## Answer sheet (open only after answering)

### 1. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-DEADLINE-NUMBER-0007`: key (A) Fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity

- Why correct: Answer: Fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity. R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(k) provides: "within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity, including bilas, inso and balae"
- (B) The Act sets the fourth degree, not the third.
- (C) Too narrow: the fourth degree, and affinity counts too.
- (D) Relatives by affinity (in-laws) are included, as are bilas, inso and balae.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(k) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity, including bilas, inso and balae"
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 2. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-DEADLINE-NUMBER-0025`: key (C) 10 years

- Why correct: Answer: 10 years. R.A. 6713, Sec. 8(C) provides: "Any statement filed under this Act shall be available to the public for a period of ten (10) years after receipt of the statement."
- (A) Ten working days is when a statement may first be copied, not how long it stays available.
- (B) Five years is the Sec. 11 maximum prison term.
- (D) One year is the post-separation period in Sec. 7(b).
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 8(C) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "Any statement filed under this Act shall be available to the public for a period of ten (10) years after receipt of the statement."
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 3. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-DEADLINE-NUMBER-0027`: key (A) ₱25,000

- Why correct: Answer: ₱25,000. R.A. 6713, Sec. 11(d) provides: "may assess against such person a penalty in any amount not to exceed twenty-five thousand pesos (P25,000)"
- (B) ₱5,000 is the maximum fine for violating Sections 7, 8 or 9.
- (C) The Act sets ₱25,000 as the ceiling.
- (D) The Act sets ₱25,000 as the ceiling.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 11(d) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "may assess against such person a penalty in any amount not to exceed twenty-five thousand pesos (P25,000)"
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 4. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-DEADLINE-NUMBER-0030`: key (D) One year

- Why correct: Answer: One year. R.A. 6713, Sec. 11(a) provides: "suspension not exceeding one (1) year"
- (A) Six months' salary is the maximum fine; the suspension can run up to one year.
- (B) Five years is the maximum prison term for violating Sections 7, 8 or 9.
- (C) The Act does not set a 90-day cap.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 11(a) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "suspension not exceeding one (1) year"
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 5. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-DEADLINE-NUMBER-0035`: key (A) 30 days after publication is completed in the Official Gazette or two newspapers

- Why correct: Answer: 30 days after publication is completed in the Official Gazette or two newspapers. R.A. 6713, Sec. 17 provides: "This Act shall take effect after thirty (30) days following the completion of its publication in the Official Gazette or in two (2) national newspapers of general circulation."
- (B) Fifteen days is the general Civil Code rule; Sec. 17 sets 30 days.
- (C) February 20, 1989 is the approval date, not the effectivity date.
- (D) Sixty days is the Sec. 9 divestment period; Sec. 17 sets 30 days.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 17 <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "This Act shall take effect after thirty (30) days following the completion of its publication in the Official Gazette or in two (2) national newspapers of general circulation."

### 6. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0002`: key (D) It falls outside the Act's definition of a "gift"

- Why correct: Answer: It falls outside the Act's definition of a "gift". R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(c) provides: "It shall not include an unsolicited gift of nominal or insignificant value not given in anticipation of, or in exchange for, a favor"
- (A) Sec. 3(c) expressly excludes an unsolicited gift of nominal or insignificant value given without any favor in view.
- (B) The SALN (Sec. 8) lists assets and liabilities; it is not a clearance for small unsolicited tokens.
- (C) No consent rule applies; the head-of-office permission in Sec. 7(d) is only for foreign travel grants.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(c) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "It shall not include an unsolicited gift of nominal or insignificant value not given in anticipation of, or in exchange for, a favor"
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 7. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0003`: key (A) A gift, because a simulated sale falls under the term

- Why correct: Answer: A gift, because a simulated sale falls under the term. R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(c) provides: "shall include a simulated sale or an ostensibly onerous disposition thereof"
- (B) Paying a token price does not cure it; Sec. 3(c) treats a simulated or ostensibly onerous sale as a gift.
- (C) A loan (Sec. 3(e)) is a separate term; nothing here is lent.
- (D) Divestment (Sec. 3(j)) is an official giving up his own conflicting interest, not receiving property.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(c) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "shall include a simulated sale or an ostensibly onerous disposition thereof"
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 8. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0004`: key (B) No; it is still "receiving any gift" since the value is not nominal

- Why correct: Answer: No; it is still "receiving any gift" since the value is not nominal. R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(d) provides: "even on the occasion of a family celebration or national festivity like Christmas, if the value of the gift is neither nominal nor insignificant"
- (A) Sec. 3(d) says the act counts "even on the occasion of" a national festivity like Christmas.
- (C) No reporting rule turns such a gift into an allowed one; the Ombudsman's Sec. 7(d) regulations cover foreign-government gifts.
- (D) Whether the giver is a natural or juridical person does not matter; the test is value and the favor in view.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(d) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "even on the occasion of a family celebration or national festivity like Christmas, if the value of the gift is neither nominal nor insignificant"
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 9. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0014`: key (D) No; for one year the lawyer cannot practice on matters before the former office

- Why correct: Answer: No; for one year the lawyer cannot practice on matters before the former office. R.A. 6713, Sec. 7(b) provides: "the professional concerned cannot practice his profession in connection with any matter before the office he used to be with, in which case the one-year prohibition shall likewise apply"
- (A) Sec. 7(b) keeps a one-year bar on practice in matters before the former office.
- (B) No CSC clearance lifts the bar; the Act fixes the one-year period.
- (C) Five years is the Sec. 11 prison term; the practice bar is one year and only for matters before the former office.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 7(b) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "the professional concerned cannot practice his profession in connection with any matter before the office he used to be with, in which case the one-year prohibition shall likewise apply"
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 10. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0015`: key (A) It may be accepted, because Congress consents to fellowship grants

- Why correct: Answer: "It may be accepted, because Congress consents to fellowship grants." R.A. 6713, Sec. 7(d) expressly includes a scholarship or fellowship grant from a foreign government among the accepted exceptions. The national-interest and head-of-office permission conditions in the next clause apply to foreign travel grants, not to this fellowship exception.
- (B) Sec. 7(d) lists foreign gifts Congress consents to, including scholarships and fellowships.
- (C) The nominal-value test is for souvenirs, item (i); fellowships are a separate item (ii).
- (D) No Senate ratification is needed; Congress already gave consent in the Act.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 7(d) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "The acceptance by a public official or employee of a gift in the nature of a scholarship or fellowship grant or medical treatment"
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 11. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0016`: key (B) Permission from the head of the engineer's office

- Why correct: Answer: Permission from the head of the engineer's office. R.A. 6713, Sec. 7(d) provides: "permitted by the head of office, branch or agency to which he belongs"
- (A) Sec. 7(d)(iii) requires the permission of the head of office, branch or agency, not the DFA.
- (C) Travel grants may be of more than nominal value; no salary cap is set.
- (D) The Ombudsman writes regulations for this subsection but does not issue case-by-case waivers under the text.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 7(d) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "permitted by the head of office, branch or agency to which he belongs"
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 12. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0019`: key (A) Jointly or separately, as they choose

- Why correct: Answer: Jointly or separately, as they choose. R.A. 6713, Sec. 8(A) provides: "Husband and wife who are both public officials or employees may file the required statements jointly or separately."
- (B) Sec. 8(A) allows either joint or separate filing.
- (C) No rank rule exists; joint filing is an option, not a requirement.
- (D) Both spouses are covered; they may simply file together or apart.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 8(A) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "Husband and wife who are both public officials or employees may file the required statements jointly or separately."
- File: `docs/research/gap-fill-2000-04.json`

### 13. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0026`: key (D) No; commercial use is barred, except news reporting by the media

- Why correct: Answer: No; commercial use is barred, except news reporting by the media. R.A. 6713, Sec. 8(D) provides: "any commercial purpose other than by news and communications media for dissemination to the general public"
- (A) Public access is for accountability; Sec. 8(D) bars commercial use and uses contrary to morals or public policy.
- (B) Paying the Sec. 8(C) fee gives access, not permission for a prohibited use.
- (C) Too strong: anyone may inspect the statements at reasonable hours under Sec. 8(C).

### 14. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0028`: key (B) Yes; the same rule applies to a partner in a partnership

- Why correct: Answer: Yes; the same rule applies to a partner in a partnership. R.A. 6713, Sec. 9 provides: "The same rule shall apply where the public official or employee is a partner in a partnership."
- (A) Sec. 9 expressly extends the rule to partners in a partnership.
- (C) Registration does not remove the conflict; Sec. 9 makes no such exception.
- (D) Sec. 9 has no majority-interest condition for partners.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 9 <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "The same rule shall apply where the public official or employee is a partner in a partnership."

### 15. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0029`: key (C) The member is not subject to any sanction under the Act

- Why correct: Answer: The member is not subject to any sanction under the Act. R.A. 6713, Sec. 10(b) provides: "who, after issuance of the opinion acts in good faith in accordance with it shall not be subject to any sanction provided in this Act"
- (A) Sec. 10(b) removes the sanction altogether for good-faith reliance.
- (B) The protection is for the person who relies on the opinion and others in a similar situation.
- (D) Sec. 10(b) gives this opinion power to the committees of Congress, not the CSC.

### 16. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0031`: key (A) Yes; proof in the administrative case is sufficient cause

- Why correct: Answer: Yes; proof in the administrative case is sufficient cause. R.A. 6713, Sec. 11(b) provides: "Any violation hereof proven in a proper administrative proceeding shall be sufficient cause for removal or dismissal of a public official or employee, even if no criminal prosecution is instituted against him."
- (B) Sec. 11(b) says removal may follow even if no criminal prosecution is instituted.
- (C) Removal is available on administrative proof alone.
- (D) The Act requires no presidential approval for dismissal.

### 17. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0032`: key (B) The same penal liabilities as the officer, tried jointly

- Why correct: Answer: The same penal liabilities as the officer, tried jointly. R.A. 6713, Sec. 11(c) provides: "shall be subject to the same penal liabilities as the public officials or employees and shall be tried jointly with them"
- (A) Sec. 11(c) expressly reaches private individuals who conspire with public officials.
- (C) The liability is penal, the same as the official's.
- (D) The supplier faces the same penal liabilities, not a fine-only rule.

### 18. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0034`: key (D) No; the Act does not derogate from more stringent standards

R.A. 6713, Sec. 13 provides: "Nothing in this Act shall be construed to derogate from any law, or any regulation prescribed by any body or agency, which provides for more stringent standards for its official and employees."
- (A) Sec. 13 keeps stricter laws and agency rules in force.
- (B) No congressional approval is required by Sec. 13.
- (C) Sec. 13 has no hiring-date condition.

### 19. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-TERM-MATCH-0001`: key (C) Government-owned or controlled corporations and their subsidiaries

- Why correct: Answer: Government-owned or controlled corporations and their subsidiaries. R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(a) provides: "including government-owned or controlled corporations, and their subsidiaries"
- (A) Receiving public funds does not make a private school part of "Government" under Sec. 3(a).
- (B) Accreditation by COMELEC does not make a party a government instrumentality; Sec. 3(a) does not list parties.
- (D) A contractor stays a private party; Sec. 3(a) covers agencies, local governments, GOCCs and their subsidiaries.

- (A) Sec. 3(e) is not limited to cash or to banks; it also covers commodatum and guarantees.

- (D) Sec. 3(e) names both simple loan and commodatum.

- (A) R.A. 6713 sets no percentage; the test is enough shares to elect a director.
- (B) A majority is not required; enough shares to elect one director is enough.

- (A) Sec. 6 gives no exemption from ratings; it gives promotion.

- (A) Military and police personnel are public officials under Sec. 3(b) and are not exempted.

### 27. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-TERM-MATCH-0024`: key (B) A reasonable fee for reproduction, mailing and certification

- Why correct: Answer: A reasonable fee for reproduction, mailing and certification. R.A. 6713, Sec. 8(C) provides: "Any person requesting a copy of a statement shall be required to pay a reasonable fee to cover the cost of reproduction and mailing of such statement, as well as the cost of certification."
- (A) The statements are open to the public, but Sec. 8(C)(3) still requires a reasonable fee.

### 28. `CIVIO-GF2K04-GI-WHO-HOLDS-POWER-0009`: key (C) The official next-in-rank or the officer in charge

- Why correct: Answer: The official next-in-rank or the officer in charge. R.A. 6713, Sec. 5(c) provides: "In the absence of duly authorized signatories, the official next-in-rank or officer in charge shall sign for and in their behalf."
- (A) Sec. 5(c) names the next-in-rank official or the officer in charge, not the legal office.
- (B) The public cannot pick a signatory; the Act names who signs.
- (D) Waiting is what Sec. 5(c) prevents: documents must be processed within a reasonable time.

- (A) The DBM Secretary is not named in Sec. 6.

- (A) The CSC administers the Act generally (Sec. 12), but Sec. 7(d) gives this rule-making to the Ombudsman.
